note: Every value this pack had to choose, in two kinds, because NIST supplies an id namespace for one kind and none for the other. Conflating them would invent a namespace where NIST already has one, and would dress deployment policy up as NIST text.

kinds.odp: A genuine NIST organization-defined parameter. The id and the sp800_53a_label are the catalog's own, read from the shipped control file at source/controls/. Value chosen by this deployment.
kinds.deployment_policy: NOT a NIST parameter. AC-3 enforces 'approved authorizations ... in accordance with applicable access control policies' but does not define those policies, and IA-2 does not define who an organizational user is. These are this deployment's rules, which AC-3 and IA-2 then enforce. They are pinned here because a verdict that turns on one is otherwise underivable.

ac-03.02_odp.nist_guideline: privileged commands and/or other actions requiring dual authorization are defined;
ac-03.02_odp.value: every action in the `extreme_risk` predicate class (predicates/index.json): two distinct non-machine identities

ac-05_odp.nist_guideline: duties of individuals requiring separation are defined;
ac-05_odp.value: proposing an action and approving it; approving and co-approving the same action

au-10_odp.nist_guideline: actions to be covered by non-repudiation are defined;

au-08_odp.nist_guideline: granularity of time measurement for audit record timestamps is defined;

policy.canonical_action_binding.value: An approval binds exactly one canonical action, identified by its payload fingerprint. Executing a different payload is not the approved authorization, whatever a trace asserts.

policy.authority_ttl_seconds.note: 24 hours, measured from the approval's decision, for an approval recording no explicit expires_at

policy.expiry_precedence.value: Where both an authority TTL and an explicit expires_at exist, the EARLIER governs. The window is CLOSED at the deadline (expires_at <= now).

policy.revocation.value: A revoked approval binds nothing from the moment of revocation.

policy.approver_standing.value: An approver whose authorization changed after approving is not an authorized individual at execution. Standing is evaluated AT EXECUTION, not at approval.

policy.organizational_hold.value: An active organizational or deployment-wide hold suspends execution. A hold is a state of the deployment and is never an event in an approval's history.

policy.one_execution.value: An approval is consumed by ONE execution. A replay is not a second authorized execution, and a second idempotency key does not create a second authorization. A REFUSAL IS NOT AN EXECUTION: a refused attempt produces no effect and consumes nothing.
policy.one_execution.note: The last sentence is pinned because T1-F7-retry-after-refusal-001's allow turns on it and the first review could not derive it.

policy.account_scope.value: An approval binds only within the account it was decided in. An execution requested by a run belonging to a different account is outside the approved authorization, even when it presents that approval's identifier, idempotency key and payload.

policy.authoritative_time_source.value: The plane's own system clock. An instant appearing in an exported trace is a PRESENTED value; where a presented instant and the system clock differ, the system clock governs.

policy.organizational_user.value: A principal with a recorded, current account membership. A principal name appearing in a trace with no membership behind it is not an organizational user and its apparent act is not a seat.

execution_rate.note: No per-principal execution burst limit is pinned, and none is derivable from AC-3, AC-3(2), AC-5, AU-8, AU-10 or IA-2: AC-7 concerns unsuccessful logon attempts and SC-5 denial of service. T4-R1-rate-limit-001 is `unresolvable` for exactly this reason, and its decisive dimension `execution_burst` deliberately feeds nothing.
